earthrise: Earthrise — the first photograph of our planet from the Moon, drawn entirely from the opening of Genesis that the Apollo 8 crew read aloud from lunar orbit on Christmas Eve 1968.
blue-marble: The Blue Marble — the whole Earth seen from Apollo 17, set entirely in the words of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
starry-night: Van Gogh's Starry Night, drawn entirely from the opening of Walt Whitman's Song of Myself.
great-wave: Hokusai's Great Wave off Kanagawa, drawn entirely from the opening chapters of Melville's Moby-Dick.
lincoln: A portrait of Abraham Lincoln, set entirely in the words of the Cooper Institute address that helped carry him to the presidency.
mona-lisa: Leonardo's Mona Lisa, drawn entirely from Walter Pater's celebrated essay on Leonardo da Vinci.
darwin: Charles Darwin, drawn entirely from the last page of On the Origin of Species — “endless forms most beautiful.”
pillars-of-creation: The Pillars of Creation, drawn entirely from H. G. Wells's 1897 story The Star.
wanderer: Caspar David Friedrich's Wanderer above the Sea of Fog, drawn entirely from the Prologue of Nietzsche's Thus Spake Zarathustra.
red-fuji: Hokusai's Red Fuji, drawn entirely from Lafcadio Hearn's essay Fuji-no-Yama.
douglass: Frederick Douglass, drawn entirely from the chapters of his Narrative in which he teaches himself to read.
twain: Mark Twain, drawn entirely from the steamboat-dreaming chapters of Life on the Mississippi.
poe: Edgar Allan Poe, drawn entirely from his tale The Fall of the House of Usher.
tesla: Nikola Tesla, drawn entirely from his own memoir My Inventions.
herschel: John Herschel, drawn entirely from his Preliminary Discourse on the Study of Natural Philosophy.
